package tungp.android.bazarbooks.mvi

import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.MutableStateFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.StateFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.asStateFlow

/**
 * Base ViewModel for MVI architecture pattern.
 * 
 * @param T The type of data that will be wrapped in BaseViewState.Data
 * @param EVENT The type of events this ViewModel will handle
 */
abstract class MviViewModel<T, EVENT> : MvvmViewModel() {

 private val _uiState = MutableStateFlow<BaseViewState<T>>(BaseViewState.Empty)
 val uiState: StateFlow<BaseViewState<T>> = _uiState.asStateFlow()

 abstract fun onTriggerEvent(eventType: EVENT)

 protected fun setState(state: BaseViewState<T>) = safeLaunch {
 _uiState.emit(state)
 }

 protected fun setData(data: T) = safeLaunch {
 _uiState.emit(BaseViewState.Data(data))
 }

 override fun startLoading() {
 super.startLoading()
 _uiState.value = BaseViewState.Loading
 }

 override fun handleError(exception: Throwable) {
 super.handleError(exception)
 _uiState.value = BaseViewState.Error(exception)
 }
}

I'll create a HorizontalPager component that uses your `SpecialOfferItem` class to display special offers with indicators. Here's how to implement it:

```kotlin:app/src/main/java/tungp/android/bazarbooks/screens/main/components/SpecialOffersCarousel.kt
package tungp.android.bazarbooks.screens.main.components

import androidx.compose.foundation.ExperimentalFoundationApi
import androidx.compose.foundation.background
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Box
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Row
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.fillMaxWidth
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.padding
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.size
import androidx.compose.foundation.pager.HorizontalPager
import androidx.compose.foundation.pager.PagerState
import androidx.compose.foundation.pager.rememberPagerState
import androidx.compose.foundation.shape.CircleShape
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.ui.Alignment
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.draw.clip
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Color
import androidx.compose.ui.tooling.preview.Preview
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import tungp.android.bazarbooks.domain.model.Book
import tungp.android.bazarbooks.domain.model.PreviewData
import tungp.android.bazarbooks.ui.theme.constants.MyColors

@OptIn(ExperimentalFoundationApi::class)
@Composable
fun SpecialOffersCarousel(
 specialOffers: List<Book>,
 onOfferItemClick: (String) -> Unit,
 modifier: Modifier = Modifier
) {
 val pagerState = rememberPagerState(pageCount = { specialOffers.size })

 Box(modifier = modifier) {
 HorizontalPager(
 state = pagerState,
 modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth()
 ) { page ->
 SpecialOfferItem(
 offerBook = specialOffers[page],
 onOfferItemClick = onOfferItemClick
 )
 }
 
 // Pager indicator
 Row(
 modifier = Modifier
 .align(Alignment.BottomCenter)
 .padding(bottom = 8.dp),
 verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically
 ) {
 repeat(specialOffers.size) { iteration ->
 val color = if (pagerState.currentPage == iteration) 
 MyColors.primary else Color.LightGray
 Box(
 modifier = Modifier
 .padding(horizontal = 4.dp)
 .size(8.dp)
 .clip(CircleShape)
 .background(color)
 )
 }
 }
 }
}

@Preview
@Composable
private fun SpecialOffersCarouselPreview() {
 SpecialOffersCarousel(
 specialOffers = PreviewData.topOfWeek.take(3),
 onOfferItemClick = {}
 )
}
```

## How to Use This Component

You can use the `SpecialOffersCarousel` in your screen/page like this:

```kotlin
@Composable
fun YourScreen(viewModel: YourViewModel) {
 // Get special offers from your viewModel or state
 val specialOffers = viewModel.specialOffers
 
 // Add the carousel to your layout
 SpecialOffersCarousel(
 specialOffers = specialOffers,
 onOfferItemClick = { isbn -> 
 // Handle the click event, e.g., navigate to book details
 viewModel.onBookSelected(isbn)
 },
 modifier = Modifier.padding(vertical = 16.dp)
 )
}
```

This implementation:
1. Creates a horizontal pager that displays one `SpecialOfferItem` at a time
2. Shows indicator dots at the bottom to show the current page and total pages
3. Updates the `SpecialOfferItem` to actually use the `onOfferItemClick` callback when the "Order Now" button is clicked
4. Uses the `Book.isbn` as the identifier when an item is clicked

The `statusBarColor` property is indeed deprecated. The modern approach in Jetpack Compose is to use the Status Bar API from Accompanist or Android's WindowCompat along with SystemUiController.

Here's how to fix this deprecation:

```kotlin
// Add this dependency to your build.gradle if not already added
// implementation "com.google.accompanist:accompanist-systemuicontroller:0.30.1"
```

Now update your code to use SystemUiController:

```kotlin:app/src/main/java/tungp/android/bazarbooks/MainActivity.kt
import androidx.compose.runtime.SideEffect
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.toArgb
import androidx.core.view.WindowCompat
import com.google.accompanist.systemuicontroller.rememberSystemUiController

class MainActivity : ComponentActivity() {
 override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
 super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
 
 // Make the system UI draw over app content
 WindowCompat.setDecorFitsSystemWindows(window, false)
 
 // Remove the deprecated line:
 // window.statusBarColor = Color.Transparent.toArgb()
 
 setContent {
 BazarBooksTheme {
 // Remember the system UI controller
 val systemUiController = rememberSystemUiController()
 val useDarkIcons = !isSystemInDarkTheme()
 
 // Update status bar colors using the SystemUiController
 SideEffect {
 systemUiController.setStatusBarColor(
 color = Color.Transparent,
 darkIcons = useDarkIcons
 )
 }
 
 // Your app content
 // ...
 }
 }
 }
}
```

This solution:

1. Uses the SystemUiController from Accompanist (Google's official set of Compose helpers)
2. Makes the system UI draw over your app content (for edge-to-edge design)
3. Sets the status bar color to transparent with appropriate icons (light/dark based on theme)
4. Applies the changes with a SideEffect to ensure they happen when the composition is successful
